title: Sound, Light and Heat Energy
seo_title: Grade 4 Science: Sound, Light and Heat Energy Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_code: Grade 4, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy
standard_text: Sound, light and heat are forms of energy. Sound is made by vibrations; light travels in straight lines and can be reflected; heat moves from hotter to cooler objects. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 4, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy): vibrations and sound, pitch and loudness, sources of light, materials and light, and heat. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Sound, light and heat are forms of energy.
key_sub: Heat moves from hot things to cold things.
body_html:
How to think about it

Sound is made when objects vibrate; it travels through air, liquids and solids. Pitch is how high or low a sound is; loudness is how strong it is.

Light travels in straight lines from a source; it passes through transparent materials and is blocked by opaque ones. Heat moves from a hotter object to a cooler one: a spoon in hot soup gets hot.

Example

Why does a metal spoon in hot soup get hot?

Heat moves.

Answer: heat moves from the soup to the spoon

Example

Which material lets light through?

Clear

Answer: clear glass

Common mistakes

  • Thinking cold moves into things.
  • Mixing up pitch and loudness.
  • Thinking light bends around corners.

faq.q: Why are pot handles made of wood or plastic?
faq.a: They do not conduct heat well, so they stay cool to hold.

faq.q: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
faq.a: Light travels much faster than sound.

items.q: Can sound travel through the string of a string telephone?
c: Yes, the vibrations can pass through it.
Only if it is very loud.
No, there are no particles to carry the vibrations.

items.q: When a drum makes a sound, what is vibrating?

items.e: All sounds are made by something vibrating.

items.q: “The vibrations travel through the air into the ear.” What happens next?

items.e: Vibration → air → eardrum → tiny bones → nerves → brain.

items.q: Which of these is a light source: a lit bulb, a sheet of white paper, the Moon or the planet Venus?

items.q: Which is an artificial source of light?
items.e: People make artificial sources.

items.q: What temperature does water freeze at?
items.e: Water boils at 100 °C at sea level.

items.q: Hot soup touches a metal spoon. Which one loses heat?
items.e: The hotter object loses heat to the colder one.

items.q: A hot iron touches a cotton shirt. In which direction does heat flow?
c: from a hot iron to a cotton shirt
from a cotton shirt to a hot iron
items.e: Heat flows from a hotter object to a colder one.

items.q: A hot pan touches the cold water poured into it. Which one loses heat?
c: the cold water poured into it
items.e: The hotter object loses heat to the colder one.

items.q: A cold can of drink touches the air in the room. Which one gains heat?

items.q: Rose compares two things. Which has more total thermal energy: a large lake (15 °C) or a hot spark (900 °C)?
c: They have the same thermal energy.
items.e: Thermal energy is the total energy of all the particles; the larger amount has far more particles.
